title: Yuman EA skill contract
description: Schema for skill.yaml. The contract a skill declares to the orchestrator, to overlays, and to CI. Prose belongs in SKILL.md; every weight, threshold, criterion, and missing-data behaviour belongs here so that an overlay can address it. Normative narrative: spec/lifecycle.md.

spec_version.description: Version of this schema the skill is written against.

id.description: Canonical skill ID: yea.<domain>.<slug> for core skills, x.<org>.<domain>.<slug> for third-party or organization skills. Must agree with the domain field and with the directory path.

slug.description: Directory name of the skill. Must equal the last segment of id. Redundant on purpose: it is what artifact filenames are derived from.

name.description: Canonical human-readable name. One name per concept — no aliases.

display_name.description: Optional friendlier label for docs and UI. The ONLY place a second label for this skill may exist.

description.description: One paragraph, functional language, no framework vocabulary. Mirrored into SKILL.md frontmatter — see spec/standard-mapping.md.

version.description: Semver, per skill. Weight or criteria change = minor. Changed artifact schema = major.

owner_agent.description: The L1 domain agent that owns this skill. Never 'orchestrator' — the router does not own methods.

license.description: SPDX identifier. Must match the repository licence for core skills.

data_intensity.description: How much organizational data the skill needs before it produces a defensible answer. low = usable with manual input and the architect's own knowledge; medium = usable with CSV exports the architect can produce unaided; high = needs a maintained repository or connector feed. Phase-1 skills are low. A skill is 'medium' or 'high' only if it CANNOT degrade honestly to manual input — see lifecycle.md R14.

deprecated.description: Set for a minimum of two releases before removal.

superseded_by.description: Skill ID that replaces this one. Required when deprecated is true.

hosts_verified.description: Agent Skills standard hosts the evals have been run against. Claude Code is the reference host; at least one other is required to promote past draft (ADR-0001 §6).

triggers.description: How the orchestrator finds this skill when the user names a problem rather than a skill. A skill with weak triggers is invisible and fails review on that basis alone (ADR-0001 §2).

phrases.description: Things a practitioner actually says, in their words, not ours. Include the colloquial forms.

decision_types.description: Coarse intent labels the orchestrator classifies to.

route_to.description: Skill ID or agent ID that should handle it instead.

not_this_skill.description: Near-miss phrases that belong somewhere else. Cheap to write, and the main defence against two skills claiming one question.

frame.description: Phase 1. Restate the user's goal as a precise EA decision statement, so the user can correct the question before any work is done.

restatement_template.description: Template with {placeholders} that resolve from ask answers and gather inputs.

decision_statement_fields.description: The placeholders the template consumes. CI checks these resolve from ask/gather IDs.

out_of_scope.description: What this skill deliberately does not decide. Stated to the user during framing.

ask.description: Phase 2. Only questions that change the answer. Maximum five, enforced here. Structured data, never prose: this block must render as a chat interview, a web form, or a batch payload without modification.

gather.description: Phase 3. Inputs, where they come from, and — for every optional input — what the skill does when it is absent. Both keys are required; use an empty array rather than omitting one.

required.description: Inputs without which the skill cannot run at all. Keep this list short: every entry is a reason the primary user gives up.

optional.description: Everything else. Each declares on_missing and a confidence penalty — degrade honestly, never demand.

bound.description: Phase 4. Constraints referenced BY POLICY ID only. Inline constraint text is rejected: an overlay cannot override prose.

policies.description: Policy IDs supplied by an overlay. A core skill declares which policies it consults; it never states what they say.

on_policy_absent.description: Behaviour when no overlay supplies a declared policy. The primary user has no overlay, so the default must be usable.

hard_constraints.description: Subset of policies that eliminate options outright rather than adjusting scores. Elimination must be reported in the artifact, never silent.

analyze.description: Phase 5. The method itself: criteria, weights, scoring scale, reasoning steps. Everything here is addressable by an overlay.

method.description: Common values: weighted_multi_criteria, matrix_placement, threshold_test, scenario_comparison, decision_tree, clustering. Not a closed enum.

criteria.description: Weights must sum to 1.0 within tolerance (lifecycle.md R7). Every criterion states what evidence scores it, so a reviewer can challenge the score rather than the vibe.

type.description: One scale for the whole skill. Mixed scales make scores incomparable and are the fastest way to lose a steering committee.

anchors.description: What each scale point means in business language. Anchors are what make a score reproducible run to run.

weights_overridable.description: Whether an overlay may change the weights. Normally true. False requires a justification in SKILL.md.

steps.description: Ordered reasoning steps. Constrain the model's procedure; do not teach it the framework.

tie_breakers.description: Applied in order when weighted scores are within the indifference band. Without these, run-to-run consistency is luck.

indifference_band.description: Score gap below which two options are reported as too close to separate, rather than ranked. Reporting a false winner is worse than reporting a tie.

subagents.description: L2 workers this skill may fan out for labour. The method stays in the skill.

references.description: Loaded on demand, not upfront. Cite external frameworks; never reproduce proprietary content.

deliver.description: Phase 6. Named artifacts with defined schemas. Every artifact declares markdown among its formats — markdown is the guaranteed floor across hosts (ADR-0001 §4).

audience.description: Who reads the output. Drives register, not content.

verify.description: Phase 7. Not quality garnish — the product. A recommendation without its assumptions, its confidence, and what would change it is a well-formatted opinion.

emits.description: The three mandatory emissions cannot be omitted. CI rejects a skill without them.

confidence_rules.description: Maps evidence state to a confidence level, so the rating is derived rather than asserted.

when.description: Checkable condition, expressed against gather inputs and their on_missing outcomes.

sensitivity_targets.description: What gets varied, by how much, and what the report says. 'Which recommendation flips at ±20% cost error' is the sentence that survives a CFO.

target.description: Criterion ID, weight, or gather input ID being varied.

report.description: What the artifact must state about the result.

evals.description: Golden cases live beside the skill. Minimum three to merge at draft (lifecycle.md R12).

skill_slug.description: Noun phrase naming the decision or the deliverable. Banned suffixes and version numbers are rejected here rather than in review. The no-gerunds rule is a lint warning, not a schema constraint — regex cannot separate 'evaluating-sourcing-options' from 'pricing-model'. See lifecycle.md R2.

domain.description: Closed enum. Extending it requires an ADR.

category.description: Closed enum of eight. Extending it requires an ADR.

maturity.description: Closed enum. Promotion criteria in lifecycle.md.

policy_ref.description: A policy ID, not a policy. The length limit exists to stop inline constraint prose.

input_source.description: Where the input comes from. connector.* names a CAPABILITY (connector.finance, connector.vendor_catalog), never a product. Vendor names are rejected by CI lint R9.

question.description: Asked in the practitioner's language. If answering it needs framework training, rewrite it.

why.description: What changes in the answer depending on the response. If you cannot write this sentence, the question does not belong in ask.

option_labels.description: Optional display text per option value, for hosts that render a form.

default_if_skipped.description: Used when the user declines or a batch payload omits the answer. Required when required is true, so the skill never deadlocks on an unanswered question.

affects.description: Criterion IDs whose weight or score this answer moves. Makes the 'only questions that change the answer' rule machine-checkable.

format.description: Shape of the input, so a CSV column mapping can be checked.

schema_ref.description: Path to a context schema this input must conform to, e.g. context/schema/application.schema.json.

on_missing.description: Closed enum. halt_with_explanation on an OPTIONAL input is a contradiction and is rejected by CI rule R6 — if absence stops the skill, the input is required.

proxy.description: The substitute used. Required when on_missing is use_proxy_metric.

assumption_template.description: The sentence written into the assumptions register when this path is taken. Required for every estimating path — an unstated assumption is the failure this whole schema exists to prevent.

confidence_penalty.description: How far the overall confidence rating drops when this input is absent. 'none' is allowed only where absence genuinely does not weaken the conclusion.

weight.description: Declared here so an overlay can address it. Never buried in prose.

description.description: What this criterion measures, in business language.

evidence.description: gather input IDs and ask IDs that produce the score. A criterion with no evidence path is an opinion with a weight on it.

applies_to.description: Restricts the criterion to a subset of options, where it is meaningless for the others.

id.description: Artifact filenames are derived, not declared: <skill-slug>--<id with underscores replaced by hyphens>.<ext>.

formats.description: Must include md. Hosts differ in whether they can write Office formats; markdown is the floor that makes the artifact real everywhere.

preferred_format.description: Used where the host supports it. Defaults to md.

template.description: Path to the rich-format template, e.g. templates/scorecard.

markdown_template.description: Path to the markdown form of this artifact, shipped with the skill.

content_schema.description: The defined schema the phase-6 contract requires. Columns for tabular artifacts, sections for documents.

always.description: Emitted on every run, even at low confidence. At least one artifact per skill must be always: true, or a run can end with nothing in the user's hands.
